key_facts: SQL is a standard computer language for relational database management and data manipulation.

SQL is divided into three sub-languages: DDL (Data Definition Language with CREATE/ALTER/DROP), DML (Data Manipulation Language with SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE), and DCL (Data Control Language with COMMIT/ROLLBACK/GRANT/REVOKE).
A schema in SQL is a group of tables and other constructs that belong to the same database application, created via 'CREATE SCHEMA Schema_Name AUTHORIZATION Authorization_Identifier'.
A catalog in SQL is a named collection of schemas.
CREATE TABLE supports column constraints (NOT NULL, UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY, DEFAULT, CHECK) and table-level constraints including FOREIGN KEY with referential actions ON UPDATE and ON DELETE.
generated_text: Introduction to Structured Query Language (SQL) Structured Query Language (SQL) is a standard computer language for relational database management and data manipulation. It is the foundation for interacting with most modern database systems. SQL commands are broadly categorized into three main sub-languages: Data Definition Language (DDL) : Used to define and manage the database structure. Data Manipulation Language (DML) : Used to manage the data within the database objects. Data Control Language (DCL) : Used to control access to the data in the database. Data Definition Language (DDL) DDL permits the specification of data types, structures, and any data constraints. These specifications are then stored in the database itself. The primary DDL commands are: CREATE : Makes a new database object (like a database, table, index, or user). ALTER : Changes the definition of a base table or other schema elements. This can include adding or dropping a column or constraint. DROP : Removes an entire database object, such as a table. For example, you can use the ALTER command to modify an existing table: -- Add a new column to the Employee table ALTER TABLE Employee ADD Job VARCHAR(15); -- Drop a column from the Employee table ALTER TABLE Employee DROP COLUMN Address CASCADE; -- Change a column's default value ALTER TABLE Department ALTER COLUMN Mgr_ssn SET DEFAULT ‘333445555’; Data Manipulation Language (DML) DML is used for retrieving, inserting, deleting, and updating data in the database. The core DML commands include: SELECT : Retrieves information from a database. It is the same as the SELECT operation in relational algebra. The basic structure of a query includes several clauses: SELECT : Specifies which columns are to appear in the output. FROM : Specifies the table(s) to be used. WHERE : Filters rows based on a condition. GROUP BY : Forms groups of rows with the same column value. HAVING : Filters groups subject to some condition. ORDER BY : Specifies the order of the output. INSERT : Adds one or more tuples (rows) to a relation (table). The attribute values should be listed in the same order as the attributes were specified in the CREATE TABLE command. INSERT INTO TableName (Attribute1, Attribute2, …) VALUES (value1, value2, …); UPDATE : Modifies attribute values of one or more selected tuples. UPDATE TableName SET Set-Clause WHERE Condition; DELETE : Removes tuples from a relation. If the WHERE clause is missing, all tuples in the relation are deleted. DELETE FROM TableName WHERE Condition; Data Control Language (DCL) DCL commands are used to manage database security and user access. The main commands are: GRANT : Passes privileges on database objects to other users. REVOKE : Takes back (cancels) privileges from other users. COMMIT : Saves all the transactions to the database. ROLLBACK : Undoes transactions that have not already been saved to the database. The syntax for granting and revoking privileges is as follows: -- Granting a privilege GRANT <privilege list> ON <database objects> TO <user list> -- Revoking a privilege REVOKE <privilege list> ON <database objects> FROM <user list> Summary This lesson provided an overview of Structured Query Language and its three core components. To recap: SQL is the standard language for managing relational databases. DDL commands ( CREATE , ALTER , DROP ) define the database schema. DML commands ( SELECT , INSERT , UPDATE , DELETE ) manipulate the data within the schema. DCL commands ( GRANT , REVOKE , COMMIT , ROLLBACK ) control data access and manage transactions.
